60-day rule: identified overpayments must be reported & returned within 60 days; 6-year lookback
Suspension of Medicare payments in whole/part on a credible allegation of fraud
Reopening of claim determinations & redeterminations to correct errors
Diagnostic lab/imaging & other tests must be ordered by the treating physician/practitioner
DMEPOS face-to-face/written order requirements

DMEPOS prior authorization requirements. Lists updated by FR notice CMS-6109-N (Jul 30, 2026): +20 Master List / +8 Required PA List HCPCS, eff Oct 28, 2026; upper-limb L3761/L3916 phased Oct 28 2026-Apr 26 2027 by state. (updated 2026-08-03)
MA plans must cover all Part A/B services available in the service area (basic benefits) and follow Traditional Medicare coverage criteria
MLR credibility adjustment: partially-credible MA contracts (2,400-180,000 member months) may add an adjustment to the medical loss ratio
MA risk-adjustment data requirements
Part C 60-day rule: MA orgs must report & return identified overpayments within 60 days; 6 most-recent completed payment years lookback
MA contract condition: adopt & implement an effective compliance program to prevent, detect & correct non-compliance and FWA; compliance officer/committee required
Part D pharmacy access: convenient retail network (urban 90% within 2 miles), any-willing-pharmacy on standard terms, out-of-network access rules
Part D drug management programs for at-risk beneficiaries (opioid/frequently-abused-drug overutilization)
Part D sponsor condition: effective compliance program (mirrors §422.503) to prevent, detect & correct non-compliance and FWA
Basic conditions a claim must meet before Medicare will pay
Providers must report enrollment changes (30/90 days) & retain ordering/referring records
Risk-based enrollment screening: limited / moderate / high categorical risk levels
Single State agency: the State plan must designate one agency to administer/supervise Medicaid; policy-making authority may not be delegated
Medicaid third-party liability: states must identify legally liable third parties and pay Medicaid last (cost avoidance) before program funds are used.
Inmate/institutional FFP exclusion (with 435.1010 definitions)
Medicaid managed-care rate setting: capitation rates must be actuarially sound (§438.4) per rate-development standards (§438.5), special contract provisions (§438.6) & rate certification (§438.7)

Sets the program-integrity duties a Medicaid managed care plan (MCO/PIHP/PAHP) must carry out under its state contract: adopt a compliance program, screen and enroll network providers to Part 455 standards, disclose ownership/prohibited affiliations, verify services were actually delivered, and report and return overpayments. Effect: pushes fraud-detection accountability onto the plan, not just the state.
Disclosure of ownership & control interests
State agency must suspend Medicaid payments on a credible allegation of fraud
All providers must be screened & enrolled
Revalidation at least every 5 years
Pre- and post-enrollment site visits for moderate- and high-risk Medicaid providers
State must screen against LEIE/DMF/exclusion databases (monthly federal databases check)

Governs State Medicaid Fraud Control Units (MFCUs) - the certified state agencies that investigate and prosecute Medicaid provider fraud and patient abuse/neglect. Sets certification, staffing, funding-match, and reporting rules a unit must meet to keep federal funding. (Ties to the NY MFCU decertification flagged in current feeds.)
Medicare Advantage (Part C) program regulations - eligibility, benefits, payments, contracts, and oversight
Voluntary Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit (Part D) regulations - eligibility, benefits, formulary, payments, and contracts
Medicaid State organization and general administration standards for the single State agency (Part 431).
Medicaid eligibility rules and financial/non-financial requirements for covered groups (Part 435).
Medicaid managed care standards - plan contracts, beneficiary protections, and managed-care program integrity (Part 438).

The core Medicaid program-integrity rule. Requires each state to run a fraud detection and investigation program and sets provider disclosure (ownership/control, business transactions, criminal convictions) and provider screening/enrollment requirements (risk-based screening levels, database checks, site visits). Subpart E carries the screening/enrollment provisions.

Requires states to run utilization control - reviews that confirm Medicaid services (especially inpatient hospital, ICF, and mental-hospital care) are medically necessary and appropriately provided. Establishes utilization review plans and inspection-of-care requirements to catch unnecessary or excessive services.
CHIP (Children's Health Insurance Program) State plan, eligibility, and administration requirements (Part 457).
Medicare Benefit Policy Manual - what Medicare covers and the conditions/limits of coverage.
Medicare Claims Processing Manual - how providers bill and how MACs adjudicate and pay claims.
Medicare Program Integrity Manual - contractor instructions for detecting/preventing fraud, waste and abuse (enrollment, medical review, overpayments).
State Medicaid Manual - CMS's operating instructions to state Medicaid agencies.
Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual (Part D) - plan sponsor operations, formulary, and program oversight.
CMS guidance to states on Medicaid & incarceration: suspend (not terminate) eligibility and bar capitated/FFS payments for incarcerated enrollees; supports successful re-entry.
NCCI's automated correct-coding edit program (PTP, MUE, add-on-code methodologies) for Medicare & Medicaid; edit files refreshed quarterly (current PTP v322r0, eff Jul 1, 2026).
Medically Unlikely Edits - per-code daily maximum units-of-service caps; separate Practitioner/OPPS/DME files, refreshed quarterly (current edition eff Jul 1, 2026).
Procedure-to-Procedure code-pair edits with modifier indicators, plus the annual NCCI Policy Manual rationale (2026 edition eff Jan 1); PTP files updated quarterly (v322r0, eff Jul 1, 2026).

The Social Security Administration's Death Master File - the authoritative federal list of reported deaths. Used as a matching source to stop or recover payments and enrollments tied to deceased beneficiaries or providers. Access to the full file is restricted (DMF/LADMF); scope and lag should be confirmed before relying on a match.

OIG's List of Excluded Individuals/Entities - the searchable database of providers barred from federal health-care programs. Federal payment is prohibited for items or services furnished by, or ordered/prescribed by, an excluded party. Refreshes roughly monthly (July 2026 file ~82,229 active entries per current feed); verify the effective date on the OIG download page before acting.

Public Assistance Reporting Information System - an interstate/federal data-matching service states must use in Medicaid eligibility determinations to detect people enrolled in more than one state or with other federal benefits (e.g., VA). Helps prevent duplicate-enrollment improper payments.

Payment Error Rate Measurement - CMS's program that measures improper-payment rates for Medicaid and CHIP using rotating state samples (fee-for-service, managed care, and eligibility components). Produces the national Medicaid/CHIP improper-payment rate reported annually (FY2025 Medicaid 6.12%).

Risk Adjustment Data Validation - CMS audits of Medicare Advantage (Part C) plans that verify enrollee diagnoses submitted for risk-adjusted payment are supported by medical records. Unsupported diagnoses drive payment recoveries; central to MA/HCC coding-integrity oversight.

Transformed Medicaid Statistical Information System - the national Medicaid/CHIP claims and eligibility data repository states submit to CMS. Serves as the analytic backbone for program-integrity monitoring, cross-state analysis, and improper-payment detection.
GAO: CMS oversight of Medicare Advantage provider-network adequacy needs strengthening to ensure enrollee access.
GAO: fundamental improvements needed in CMS's recovery of improper Medicare Advantage payments driven by unsupported diagnoses.
GAO: CMS should assess the medical-record documentation needed to identify Medicare/Medicaid improper payments.
GAO: additional CMS data and oversight needed to ensure Medicaid children receive recommended EPSDT screenings.
GAO: action needed so CMS completes Medicaid Financial Management Reviews of state spending in a timely manner.
GAO: CMS should monitor how manufacturer drug rebates affect Medicare Part D plan formularies and beneficiary spending.
GAO: CMS oversight and guidance could improve the Medicaid Recovery Audit Contractor program, including how state exemptions from RAC review are documented and monitored.
GAO: states need additional oversight of Medicaid managed-care plans' prior-authorization decisions for children's EPSDT services, given plan incentives to deny.
GAO: enhanced cross-state data matching (e.g., via PARIS) could help prevent duplicate Medicaid, CHIP and APTC coverage and yield substantial savings.
GAO: Medicare national coverage determinations are generally timely, but CMS should identify the causes of delays and publish its analysis-prioritization criteria.
OIG: Medicare overpaid for physician services billed at higher nonfacility rates while enrollees were facility inpatients; CMS should recover overpayments and prevent place-of-service miscoding.
OIG: nearly all states made Medicaid managed-care capitation payments for beneficiaries concurrently enrolled in two states; stronger cross-state matching is needed.

OIG audit A-06-21-05003 (issued 09/19/2022). Critical access hospitals (CAHs) and practitioners were both paid for the SAME professional services; MACs overpaid providers ~$907,438 and beneficiaries were overcharged ~$281,321 in cost-sharing. Illustrates duplicate/same-service payment risk. Draft - verify against oig.hhs.gov region6/62105003.

OIG audit A-09-20-03016 (issued 05/31/2022). Of ~$40.1M paid for Power Mobility Device (PMD) repairs (FY2019), OIG estimated ~$8M improperly paid for repairs not meeting Medicare requirements. Draft - verify against oig.hhs.gov region9/92003016.

OIG audit A-09-21-03021 (issued 05/02/2023). Of ~$1B paid for psychotherapy incl. telehealth in the first COVID-19 PHE year, OIG estimated ~$580M improper ($348M telehealth, $232M non-telehealth) - e.g., undocumented time, missing signatures. Draft - verify against oig.hhs.gov region9/92103021.

OIG audit A-09-22-03005 (issued 08/17/2023). Up to ~$17.8M in potentially improper payments to opioid treatment programs (OTPs) for opioid-use-disorder services: duplicate weekly bundles ($10.4M), take-home supplies covered by other payments ($5.1M), no OUD diagnosis ($1.3M), excess intake activities ($1M); CMS had not directed MACs to add system edits. Draft - verify against oig.hhs.gov region9/92203005.

OIG audit A-09-22-03010 (issued June 2023). CMS/MAC oversight of the highest-paid molecular pathology genetic test (CPT 81408) was inadequate to reduce risk of up to ~$888M in improper payments (weak provider-relationship, disease-to-gene, and volume monitoring). Draft - verify against oig.hhs.gov region9/92203010.

OIG A-09-23-03016 (Sep 8, 2023): Medicare improperly paid acute-care hospitals ~$41.4M for inpatient claims subject to the post-acute-care transfer policy due to incorrect discharge status codes; CMS system edits became effective by period end. Supports transfer-policy/discharge-status billing edits. (added 2026-08-03)

OIG hospital compliance audit (cited as A-12-00-00503; official ID appears to be A-01-12-00503, issued 11/30/2012, Tufts Medical Center). Judgmentally sampled at-risk inpatient/outpatient claims found billing errors; hospital accepted findings and processed adjustments via its MAC. Draft - confirm the exact report ID and findings against oig.hhs.gov region1/11200503.pdf.

OIG rollup audit (cited as A-42109005; official ID appears to be A-04-21-09005, issued 11/24/2023). Across 14 prior state audits, Medicaid agencies made >$249M ($172M federal share) in unallowable capitation payments to MCOs on behalf of DECEASED enrollees; OIG recommends routine T-MSIS-to-SSA Death Master File matching. Draft - confirm ID/findings against oig.hhs.gov A-04-21-09005.
OIG: early results showed enhanced enrollment screening of Medicare providers was not fully implemented (no MAC verified all applicant identifiers); CMS concurred with all recommendations.

OIG: Unified Program Integrity Contractors (UPICs) show promise across Medicare and Medicaid but performed far less Medicaid, especially managed-care, program-integrity work than their funding implied.

OIG: ACA-required enhanced Medicaid provider-enrollment screenings (fingerprint-based background checks, site visits) were not fully implemented; states needed CMS guidance and a shared results system.

OIG OEI-09-18-00260 (Apr 27, 2022): 'Some Medicare Advantage Organization Denials of Prior Authorization Requests Raise Concerns About Beneficiary Access to Medically Necessary Care.' Found 13% of PA denials were for services that met Medicare coverage rules (~85,000/yr). Supports MA prior-auth denial-appropriateness monitoring. (added 2026-08-03)
OIG: some Medicare Advantage prior-authorization and payment denials in fact met Medicare coverage rules, raising concerns that capitated incentives restrict access to medically necessary care.
